summary: The Combat Veterans Retirement Restoration Act allows certain military disability retirees with combat-related disabilities to concurrently receive both veterans' disability compensation and retired pay, modifying existing restrictions and authorizing appropriations to fund the changes.

affected_groups.effect: May receive both standard retired pay based on uniformed services service and veterans' disability compensation without certain offsets.
affected_groups.group: Combat-related disability retirees with 20 or more years of service

affected_groups.effect: May receive the lesser of specific combined calculations of chapter 61 retired pay and disability compensation or a formula based on 20 years of service.
affected_groups.group: Combat-related disability retirees with less than 20 years of service

key_provisions: Allows combat-related disability retirees with 20 or more years of service to receive both their standard retired pay and veterans' disability compensation without specific statutory offsets.
Provides concurrent receipt formulas and limits for combat-related disability retirees with less than 20 years of service.
Excludes chapter 61 retirees who do not meet the specified combat-related or service criteria from the general concurrent receipt provisions.
Authorizes an appropriation of $9,400,000,000 to the Secretary of Defense to carry out the amendments, remaining available until expended.
Sets the effective date of the amendments for payments beginning on or after January 1, 2027.
missing_information: The exact number of individual veterans or retirees who will qualify for or receive payments under these new rules is not specified in the text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Combat Veterans Retirement Restoration Act allows certain military disability retirees with combat-related disabilities to concurrently receive both veterans' disability compensation and retired pay, modifying existing restrictions and authorizing appropriations to fund the changes.
summary_detail.significance: The bill provides retroactive funding of $9,400,000,000 and alters financial pay structures for military members retired due to disabilities resulting from combat, starting January 1, 2027.
